result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: An answer must contain a general or specific denial of the material allegations the defendant disputes.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.

claims.claim: An answer must state any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: Each defense must be stated separately.
claims.quote: The defenses shall be separately stated

claims.claim: The defenses must identify which causes of action they answer so the defenses can be told apart.
claims.quote: the several defenses shall refer to the causes of action which they are intended to answer, in a manner by which they may be intelligibly distinguished.

claims.claim: Whether a general denial is enough depends on the complaint.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient

claims.claim: A general denial is sufficient if the complaint is not verified.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient

claims.claim: A general denial is sufficient if the complaint is subject to Article 2, starting at Section 90 of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1, subject to the draft’s verified assigned-claim exception.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient
claims.note: The draft states the exception in its third bullet.

claims.claim: A general denial puts only the material allegations of the complaint in issue.
claims.quote: a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.

claims.claim: For a verified complaint outside Article 2, denial must be positive or according to the defendant’s information and belief.
claims.quote: If the complaint is verified, unless the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant.

claims.claim: For a claim assigned to a third party for collection, if the complaint is verified, denial must be positive or according to the defendant’s information and belief even when Article 2 applies.
claims.quote: However, if the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1.

claims.claim: Section 337 sets a four-year limit for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument.
claims.note: Checked within the stated scope of unsecured written contracts.

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to the exception in Section 336a.
The cited form is Judicial Council form PLD-050, revised January 1, 2024.
claims.quote: Judicial Council form PLD-050 (General Denial), Rev. January 1, 2024

claims.claim: Item 2 of PLD-050 provides space for the defendant to state facts as separate affirmative defenses to the plaintiff’s complaint.
claims.quote:
2.  DEFENDANT states the following FACTS as separate affirmative defenses to plaintiff's complaint (attach additional
pages if necessary):
claims.note: This describes the item; it does not claim every defendant may use the form.

result.summary: The provided texts support the pleading requirements, the four-year limit and its stated exception within the unsecured-contract scope, and the description of item 2 on PLD-050.
